articles.title: Absolute neutrophil count and adverse drug reaction monitoring during clozapine treatment: consensus guidelines from a global Delphi panel.
articles.snippet: Siskind D, Northwood K, Pillinger T, Chan S, Correll C, Cotes RO et al. | The lancet. Psychiatry | 2026-Jan | Journal Article; Review
articles.full_summary: This global Delphi study established consensus guidelines for ANC thresholds for clozapine cessation and monitoring protocols, recommending lowering ANC thresholds and discontinuing routine ANC monitoring after 2 years.
articles.key_finding: Recommendations include lowering ANC thresholds for consideration of clozapine cessation to 1·0 × 109 cells per L (0·5 × 109 cells per L for Duffy antigen receptor for chemokines-null individuals) and discontinuing routine ANC monitoring after 2 years.

articles.title: Clozapine-related neutropenia and agranulocytosis in Korea: 2025 update for rethinking the role of monitoring system.
articles.snippet: Kang N, Jang JS, Joo SW, Lee JH, Jeong JH, Kim M et al. | Therapeutic advances in psychopharmacology | 2026 | Journal Article
articles.full_summary: This retrospective cohort study in Korea found that clozapine-induced agranulocytosis is rare (0.17%), abrupt, and confined to the early period of treatment, suggesting a need to reconsider current hematological monitoring regulations.
articles.key_finding: Ten cases of agranulocytosis were identified, of which four (0.17%) were clozapine-related. All appeared abruptly within 5 weeks of initiation without preceding neutropenia or low baseline ANC, and recovered after discontinuation.
articles.population: patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders who had newly initiated clozapine in Korea

articles.full_summary: This FDA drug label for clozapine highlights severe neutropenia as a boxed warning, detailing baseline ANC requirements before initiation and dosage modifications based on ANC levels during treatment.
articles.key_finding: Clozapine has caused severe neutropenia which is associated with an increased risk of serious and potentially fatal infections.

articles.title: Clozapine-induced neutropenia: Prevalence and associated factors.

articles.full_summary: This retrospective study in France found a clozapine-induced agranulocytosis prevalence of 0.28% with no fatalities, and a neutropenia prevalence of 9.22%, suggesting a looser approach to hematological monitoring.
articles.key_finding: Among 1768 patients treated with clozapine, we identified 5 cases of CIA (prevalence: 0.28%), with no fatalities, and 163 cases of CIN (prevalence: 9.22%), including 36 moderate cases.

articles.full_summary: This retrospective cohort study in the UAE found that agranulocytosis did not occur in any of the 179 clozapine patients. Low ANC was uncommon and associated with baseline ANC and benign ethnic neutropenia risk.
articles.key_finding: Among 239 patients, 179 formed the final study cohort, contributing 284.7 on-clozapine person-years. articles.title: Distinctive pattern of neutrophil count change in clozapine-associated, life-threatening agranulocytosis.
articles.snippet: Taylor D, Vallianatou K, Whiskey E, Dzahini O, MacCabe J | Schizophrenia (Heidelberg, Germany) | 2022-Mar-14 | Journal Article
articles.full_summary: This study identified 9 episodes of life-threatening agranulocytosis (LTA) among clozapine patients, characterized by a distinct pattern of rapid neutrophil count decline and delayed recovery, suggesting that not all recorded agranulocytosis cases are life-threatening or clozapine-related.
articles.key_finding: We found 23 episodes recorded as agranulocytosis in clozapine patients. Of these, nine met pre-defined criteria and were considered episodes of life-threatening agranulocytosis (LTA).

articles.title: ACKR1/Duffy-null genotype testing for clozapine: A guideline developed by the UK Centre of Excellence in Regulatory Science and Innovation in Pharmacogenomics (CERSI-PGx).
articles.snippet: Murtough S, Stellakis O, Mills D, Bjourson B, Chaplin V, Chauhan D et al. | British journal of clinical pharmacology | 2026-Jul | Journal Article; Practice Guideline
articles.full_summary: This guideline proposes a framework for ACKR1 genotype testing to identify individuals with benign ethnic neutropenia (ADAN) to avoid unnecessary clozapine discontinuation and allow for revised ANC monitoring thresholds.
articles.key_finding: We recommend that people with the Duffy-null genotype should be monitored using revised WBC/ANC thresholds for ADAN.
articles.population: people starting clozapine or with below-threshold blood results in the UK

articles.title: Time for a change to clozapine haematological monitoring.
articles.snippet: Cheng A, Buten S, Large M | Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists | 2024-Aug | Journal Article; Review
articles.full_summary: This review critiques current Australian clozapine haematological monitoring guidelines, suggesting they are not consistent with current evidence. It proposes modifications like adjusting neutrophil thresholds for benign ethnic neutropenia and reducing monitoring frequency after two years.
articles.key_finding: Contemporary Australian protocols for clozapine haematological monitoring are not consistent with the current evidence base.

response.global_summary:
Clozapine, an antipsychotic medication, carries a known risk of severe neutropenia and agranulocytosis, which can lead to serious and potentially fatal infections [2]. Agranulocytosis, a severe drop in white blood cells, has been observed in patients receiving clozapine, with some cases resulting in death from infectious complications [6]. A 2026 cohort study in Korea identified four clozapine-related agranulocytosis cases (0.17%) among newly initiated patients, all appearing abruptly within five weeks of initiation without preceding neutropenia or low baseline ANC [1]. Similarly, a 2026 cohort study in Paris found a prevalence of 0.28% for clozapine-induced agranulocytosis (CIA) and 9.22% for clozapine-induced neutropenia (CIN) among 1768 patients, with no fatalities from CIA [3]. Another study identified nine episodes of life-threatening agranulocytosis among clozapine patients [5].

There is an ongoing discussion regarding the optimal absolute neutrophil count (ANC) monitoring requirements for patients on clozapine. Consensus guidelines from a global Delphi panel in 2026 recommend lowering ANC thresholds for considering clozapine cessation to **1.0 × 10^9 cells per L** (or **0.5 × 10^9 cells per L** for Duffy antigen receptor for chemokines-null individuals) and discontinuing routine ANC monitoring after two years [0]. This is supported by a 2026 clinical guideline from the UK Centre of Excellence in Regulatory Science and Innovation in Pharmacogenomics, which recommends revised WBC/ANC thresholds for individuals with the Duffy-null genotype [7].

However, some evidence suggests that current monitoring protocols may be overly cautious or not aligned with contemporary data. A 2024 review highlights that contemporary Australian protocols for clozapine haematological monitoring are **not consistent with the current evidence base** [8]. A multi-ethnic retrospective cohort study from the United Arab Emirates involving 179 patients over 284.7 on-clozapine person-years found that **88.3%** had no post-initiation ANC below 2.0 × 10^9/L, and none reached the agranulocytosis range [4]. This study suggests that the incidence of severe neutropenia and agranulocytosis might be lower than conventionally assumed in certain populations [4].

Despite the risks, a 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis found **no strong predictors** of clozapine-associated blood dyscrasia [9]. This suggests that identifying individuals at high risk for these adverse events remains challenging.

key_findings.text: Clozapine treatment is associated with a risk of severe neutropenia and agranulocytosis, which can lead to serious and potentially fatal infections.
Agranulocytosis cases related to clozapine can appear abruptly within weeks of initiation without preceding neutropenia or low baseline ANC.
The prevalence of clozapine-induced agranulocytosis (CIA) has been reported at 0.17% in Korea and 0.28% in a Paris cohort, with clozapine-induced neutropenia (CIN) at 9.22% in the latter.

Consensus guidelines recommend lowering ANC thresholds for clozapine cessation to 1.0 × 10^9 cells per L (0.5 × 10^9 cells per L for Duffy-null individuals) and discontinuing routine ANC monitoring after two years.
Individuals with the Duffy-null genotype should be monitored using revised WBC/ANC thresholds due to their increased risk for benign ethnic neutropenia.
No strong predictors of clozapine-associated blood dyscrasia have been identified.

disagreements.issue: Consistency of current clozapine haematological monitoring protocols with the evidence base
positions: Current monitoring protocols are not consistent with the evidence base and may be overly cautious, with a low incidence of severe neutropenia/agranulocytosis observed in some populations.
Clozapine carries a significant risk of severe neutropenia and agranulocytosis, necessitating careful monitoring, and revised, but still present, monitoring thresholds are recommended.

evidence_gaps: The sources do not provide specific details on the long-term outcomes or management strategies for patients who experience clozapine-induced neutropenia or agranulocytosis beyond discontinuation of the drug.
The sources do not detail the specific characteristics or risk factors that differentiate patients who experience life-threatening agranulocytosis from those with less severe neutropenic events.
The sources do not provide a comprehensive comparison of the efficacy and safety of different monitoring protocols across diverse global populations.
